paragraphs: [Eduyot 8:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Eduyot.8.1) mentions his testimony concerning red-heifer ashes, followed by “R' Akiva added,” etc. [Chagigah 23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.23b.9) cites it as well.

Hyman gives Shimon ben Pegora as the reading at the beginning of [Tosefta Eduyot, chapter 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Eduyot.3.2). He writes ובל״ם [in context, “without doubt”] that Shimon belonged to the descendants of the Bnei Beteira, who were nesiim before Hillel. He bases this on Shimon appearing alongside R’ Yehoshua ben Beteira in the Tosefta.[^4]

notes.text: Afar chatat here means red-heifer ashes used for purification. The Pegora/Petora name difference and the printed ובל״ם and מב״ב sigla remain open; the descendant reading is Hyman’s asserted conclusion, not a new genealogical record.

No new primary scalar was returned. Afar Chatat means red-heifer purification ashes, not ordinary sin-offering ashes. Supplied ובל״ם remains explicit beside a contextual without-doubt reading; cross-notice patterns do not prove a mem/samekh glyph error. The force of Hyman's asserted genealogy is preserved under that qualified reading, while מב״ב as descendants remains an uncertain expansion. Pegora/Petora and Batira/Beteira spellings are not silently harmonized. Nesiim is the leadership designation, not simply unspecified leadership; the genealogical conclusion remains Hyman's, without an authority merge. The supplied heading has abbreviated ר׳ despite the catalog's full רבי, so titles remain R'.

Mishnah Eduyot 8:1 and Chagigah 23b name Shimon ben Beteira in the testimony about red-heifer ashes, followed by Akiva’s addition. The consulted Machon Mamre Tosefta places a statement by Shimon ben Beteira after Yehoshua ben Beteira’s testimony at 3:2. The name Pegora belongs to Hyman’s report. The source’s ובל״ם and מב״ב are interpreted from context, and the proposed descent from the pre-Hillel leaders remains Hyman’s conclusion.

The linked Tosefta also reads Shimon ben Beteira after Yehoshua ben Beteira. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3417&lang=en) records the testimony and connects the name with the Bnei Beteira. The proposed family connection and the reported Pegora reading retain their attributions.
